questions.q: Which real MDM product is described in this lesson as cloud-native and built on a graph data model, with relationship/hierarchy modeling as a first-class feature?
options: Reltio
SAP Master Data Governance
Microsoft SQL Server Master Data Services
Informatica MDM
questions.explain: The lesson describes Reltio as a cloud-native, SaaS MDM platform built on a graph data model, marketed around real-time data and built-in relationship modeling.

questions.q: What happens to Microsoft SQL Server Master Data Services (MDS) starting with SQL Server 2025, per this lesson?
options: It is removed; Microsoft continues to support it only in SQL Server 2022 and earlier
It becomes the only supported MDM tool from Microsoft going forward
It is renamed Microsoft Purview with no functional change
It merges with Informatica MDM into one joint product
questions.explain: The lesson notes MDS is removed starting SQL Server 2025, continuing to be supported only in SQL Server 2022 and earlier — a reminder that tool landscapes shift.

questions.q: In the Master Data Services diagram shown in this lesson, what does the Subcategory attribute on the Product entity represent?
options: A domain-based attribute — drawn from another entity, the same kind of relationship covered in the Hierarchies lesson
A free-form text attribute with no connection to any other entity
A reference data code list unrelated to the Product model
An error state shown when the model fails to update
questions.explain: The lesson explains Subcategory is a domain-based attribute drawn from another entity — exactly the hierarchy relationship concept from Lesson 16.

questions.q: Which of these is listed in this lesson as a concrete criterion for evaluating MDM tools against each other?
options: Whether the tool supports the architecture style you actually chose
The tool vendor's total number of social media followers
Whether the tool's logo uses the color blue
How many years ago the company was founded, regardless of product fit
questions.explain: The lesson lists domain coverage, architecture style fit, matching engine quality, integration support, ecosystem fit, and deployment/cost model as the real evaluation criteria — not brand recognition.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say 'which tool' is a late question in an MDM program, not a first question?
options: Because a tool implements a strategy rather than creating one, and without the Chapter 1-4 groundwork there's nothing correct to configure
Because all MDM tools are functionally identical, so the choice doesn't matter
Because tools should always be picked before any domain or architecture decisions are made
Because MDM tools cannot be evaluated until after they are purchased
questions.explain: An organization that hasn't defined master data, picked an architecture style, designed matching rules, and scoped domains will struggle with any tool, because the tool has no correct strategy to implement yet.
